Notes

stop watchin' the news

The intro quotes Ethel Cain’s “Nettles” (2025). Cain recites these same two sung lines in her own Genius Verified breakdown. Discussing that song, she describes love becoming frightening because there is now someone to lose. That context sits beside this song’s opening fear of losing everything, before Jack turns toward gratitude and protecting the people close to him.

  • Ethel Cain explains and recites Nettles — Genius Verified
  • Genius's published video transcript (02:54–03:08 and 07:22–07:30)
  • Ethel Cain: official Nettles visualizer
  • Genius community transcript: Blessed
brown eyes look so blue

“Blue” means sad as well as the color. The eyes remain brown; what changes is the grief visible in them. The color-word contradiction gives the sampled line its force, following the suggestion to stop watching upsetting news.

  • Ethel Cain recites the line in Genius Verified, 07:30
  • Genius community transcript: Blessed
点点滴滴

点点滴滴 gathers the tiny, scattered details of life into one phrase; its repeated syllables make the accumulation audible. 小心翼翼 then means extremely carefully. The refrain treats everyday moments like fragile things that can be gathered and kept.

  • Ministry of Education dictionary: 點點滴滴
  • Ministry of Education dictionary: 小心翼翼
  • Chinese lyric transcript
果实

果实 means both literal fruit and the results earned through effort, much like 'the fruits of my labor.' The line claims those achievements as his own. The following lines shift their value toward the well-being of friends and family.

  • Ministry of Education dictionary: 果實
  • Chinese lyric transcript
幸福

幸福 is happiness understood as a good, fulfilling life, rather than only a passing cheerful mood. “Blessed” fits the gratitude and prayer around it, but the Chinese word itself does not specify a religious blessing. Friends and family doing well are the concrete measure of that happiness here.

  • Lyric text
画卷

画卷 is a pictorial scroll and, figuratively, an unfolding scene. Everyone’s name is written onto this one; the speaker will preserve it and make sure each person is looked after. The image changes private success into something deliberately kept for a whole circle of people. In a June 2025 interview about the earlier Above & Beyond, Jackzebra similarly described collecting producer friends into a picture album, with lyrics as his annotations. That earlier explanation offers a parallel to this image, rather than identifying the people in this song.

  • Jackzebra on Above & Beyond, Sabukaru, June 2025
  • Lyric text
芳名

芳名 can mean a good reputation or a person's name spoken with respect. Paired with 永存, 'endure forever,' it gives the blessing a ceremonial register. The friends and family just pictured together become people whose names deserve to last.

  • Ministry of Education dictionary: 芳名
  • Chinese lyric transcript
妖魔鬼怪

This four-part grouping piles up supernatural beings—demons, devils, ghosts, and monsters. It can also be used figuratively for sinister people or forces. Leaving it as creatures in English keeps the protective, almost spell-like form of the request without deciding which everyday dangers it means.

  • Lyric text
跪下来

Here the speaker lowers himself to ask for protection for others. “Kai” later orders somebody else onto their knees; “Throat” returns to pleading before a Buddha. Kneeling changes meaning with who is speaking and who must kneel: devotion, dominance, and desperation are distinct uses across the mixtape.

  • Kai lyric text
  • Throat lyric text
  • Lyric text
祈祷祷告

The pronoun changes to 您, the respectful form of 'you.' Just before it, 合十 describes palms and all ten fingers joined before the chest, a gesture of reverence with Buddhist associations. The paired verbs 祈祷 and 祷告 intensify the act of praying; the addressee remains unnamed.

  • Ministry of Education dictionary: 您
  • Ministry of Education dictionary: 合十
  • Ministry of Education dictionary: 祈禱
  • Chinese lyric transcript
